evidence: Source review of the pinned SDK plus an executed adapted C++ probe for CPP-184, CPP-185 and CPP-189. Public Rust handling is implemented in the S0 connector; native validation is recorded separately. Private extraction helpers remain unported.

entries.title: SqliteConnector permits copying an owned database handle
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Copy an open connector and destroy both copies.
entries.issue: The implicit copy duplicates db_ without ownership transfer; both destructors call sqlite3_close_v2 on the same handle. Assignment also loses the previous handle.
entries.proposed_fix: Delete copy operations and provide explicit move ownership if needed.
entries.rust_handling: SqliteConnector owns a rusqlite Connection and implements neither Clone nor Copy. Dropping an uncommitted connection rolls back through SQLite ownership; no duplicate raw handle API is exposed.

entries.title: SqliteConnector does not close a handle when opening fails
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Construct a connector for a missing read-only database or an inaccessible path.
entries.issue: sqlite3_open_v2 may return an allocated error handle. The constructor stores it then throws; the object destructor is not run, leaving that handle unclosed.
entries.proposed_fix: Close any returned handle before throwing, or use an owning local guard until successful construction.
entries.rust_handling: Connection::open_with_flags owns failed-open cleanup. Missing read-only/read-write files are rejected and remain absent. Native tests check failures and later successful opening; they do not measure allocator leaks.

entries.title: SQLite bound statements leak on bind or step errors
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Supply more blobs than placeholders, or violate a UNIQUE constraint during the step.
entries.issue: Both error branches throw before sqlite3_finalize; the source TODO acknowledges the leak. The statement may also retain borrowed SQLITE_STATIC buffers.
entries.proposed_fix: Use a statement RAII guard on all exits; bind owned data or ensure it outlives the statement.
entries.rust_handling: Prepared statements are owned RAII values. Excess bindings, constraint errors and returned rows report errors and release the statement. Native regression tests verify that subsequent queries and bindings remain usable.

entries.title: SQLite table-name helpers interpolate names as SQL syntax
entries.status: Reproduced in an executed adapted C++ probe; not a full SDK build
entries.trigger: Create a table whose name contains an apostrophe or SQL punctuation, then query it by its actual name.
entries.issue: tableExists inserts the name into a quoted literal without escaping; countTableRows and columnExists insert an unquoted identifier. Valid names can fail or alter the query meaning.
entries.proposed_fix: Bind values such as sqlite_master.name and correctly quote SQL identifiers with doubled double quotes.
entries.rust_handling: table_exists binds its name as a value; count_table_rows and column_exists quote the entire identifier and double embedded quotes. Native tests cover punctuation-bearing names, injection-shaped input and NUL identifier rejection.
adapted_probe_observations: The ordinary table T exists; ABSENT does not.
The existing table named odd'name causes IllegalArgument during preparation.
The absent literal name "ABSENT' OR 1=1 --" incorrectly returns true.
The existing table named "odd table" causes preparation errors in both row-count and column-existence queries.

entries.title: SQLite query helpers ignore step errors and can leak statements
entries.status: Reproduced in an executed adapted C++ probe; not a full SDK build
entries.trigger: Cause sqlite3_step to return SQLITE_BUSY or another error while querying an existing table.
entries.issue: The helpers inspect column types without checking the step result. Existence queries can conflate an execution error with absence; countTableRows throws on NULL before finalizing. The adapted probe reproduced this with an exclusive lock after a warm read.
entries.proposed_fix: Check SQLITE_ROW/DONE explicitly, report other statuses, and finalize through RAII.
entries.rust_handling: Every query checks rusqlite preparation and row-step results; errors propagate as Error::Io rather than false. Owned statements clean up on all exits. Native locked-query tests cover all three operations and successful reuse after unlocking.
adapted_probe_observations: After a warm read returns 3 rows, a second connection holds BEGIN EXCLUSIVE.
A direct trace records successful preparation (SQLITE_OK, 0) followed by SQLITE_BUSY (5) at step.
Both tableExists(T) and columnExists(T, ID) return false, with database error code 5.
countTableRows(T) throws the adapted SqlOperationFailed and leaves one outstanding statement, counted using sqlite3_next_stmt.
After the second connection rolls back, the count is again 3.

entries.title: SQLite string extraction truncates embedded NUL bytes
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Extract a SQLite TEXT value containing bytes a, NUL, b.
entries.issue: The helper constructs std::string from a C string and loses bytes after the first NUL.
entries.proposed_fix: Use sqlite3_column_bytes with the returned pointer and retain an explicit byte length.
entries.rust_handling: The S0 public connector is implemented, but the private extraction helper remains unported. Binary-binding tests preserve NUL bytes; they are not evidence for a text-extraction replacement.

entries.title: SQLite integer-to-string extraction narrows to 32 bits
entries.status: Source-reviewed candidate; not reproduced in running C++
entries.trigger: Read the SQLite INTEGER value 4294967297 through extractValueIntStr.
entries.issue: The helper uses sqlite3_column_int despite SQLite INTEGER being signed 64-bit; conversion to text follows an already narrowed value.
entries.rust_handling: The S0 public connector is implemented, but the private integer-to-string extraction helper remains unported. Row counts use a checked i64-to-usize conversion; no extraction-helper correction is claimed.

entries.title: SqliteConnector row-count documentation names the wrong exception
entries.status: Reproduced in an executed adapted C++ probe; not a full SDK build
entries.trigger: Call countTableRows("UNKNOWN") on a database without that table.
entries.issue: Header promises SqlOperationFailed; prepareStatement throws IllegalArgument, and the class test explicitly expects IllegalArgument.
entries.proposed_fix: Correct the header to document IllegalArgument for an unknown table, or deliberately translate the error and update the test as an API change.
entries.rust_handling: The native rustdoc and support document state the source mismatch and specify Error::Io with an underlying SQLite cause for an absent table. The source class-test expectation is mapped to a native error regression.
entries.evidence: Pinned source and class-test review; SqliteConnector.cpp82,145-153 and SqliteConnector_test.cpp105-106. Files hashed in sqlite_connector_provenance.json.
adapted_probe_observations: countTableRows(UNKNOWN) throws the adapted IllegalArgument from the exact pinned prepareStatement path, agreeing with the source class test and contradicting the installed header.
Substitute exception classes preserve distinct throw/catch paths; the original exception inheritance, ABI and metadata formatting are not exercised.

external_reference_note: Adapted C++ probe on kim. Exact pinned SqliteConnector.cpp/.h/_impl.h and sqlite3.h declarations; small support substitutes for StandardTypes, Exception and StringUtils. Host SQLite3.45.1 shared library. Not full OpenMS SDK include/link closure or original exception ABI.

adapted_probe_execution.linkage: Host system libsqlite3.so.0; development headers absent, exact pinned SQLite declaration header used. No SQLite implementation source compiled and no library downloaded.
